prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1221; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a rear-end collision. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office. The driver is named on the policy and coverage is being confirmed.

Entry 2: The claimant's attorney sent the initial injury notice describing whiplash. The file has no medical records yet, and it is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.

Entry 3: Police confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. Nothing independent confirms the accident itself: there are no witnesses to the impact, no photos and no other report.

Entry 4: The claimant's account has changed between conversations. The direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now described differently than in the first call.

Entry 5: Inspection shows vehicle damage that matches the impact described. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known to us. A neighbor has mentioned seeing the car damaged some weeks before the claimed loss, and I am following up on that.

Entry 6: The medical records show a small strain in the same area several years ago, which healed fully. Treatment after this claim followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.

Entry 7: File is being prepared for review with the injury question still open. Next steps are to request complete prior records and to schedule a recorded statement with the claimant through counsel.
